name: sol_mccc_11
description: Unsafe assumption of constant block time/production rate in cross-chain logic
question: The source file in `source` computes time-based logic (e.g., deadlines, unlock periods, reward rates, or vesting) by multiplying block.number differences by a fixed assumed block time or interval, instead of using block.timestamp or an oracle, so that on chains with inconsistent or variable block production the computed duration is wrong; this excludes code that only uses block.timestamp directly or that documents the fixed-block-time chain as the sole deployment target with no cross-chain intent.
criteria: A function computes elapsedTime or duration as (block.number - startBlock) * AVERAGE_BLOCK_TIME to determine deadlines or unlocks
Reward or interest accrual rate is calculated per block assuming a fixed number of blocks per day/year without adjusting for actual timestamps
A cross-chain or multi-chain module estimates matching finality/time windows using block counts calibrated to one chain's known block interval
Vesting or staking logic converts a fixed block count into a real-world time duration using a hardcoded blocks-per-second constant
